description: the main data used for start page with the global problems and most effizient solutions. Contains also the words and triples with description and reference used for unit testing to fix the id that are not part of the other files loaded before the config.yaml. The potential loss values are own estimates in trillion EUR per year, each with a basis in the note and a separate confidence value; they replace the earlier values that were derived from the htp share.

triples.name: wealth concentration
triples.description: concentration of money and power that destroys democratic participation (concept paper section 5)

triples.name: market power
triples.description: the ability of a market dominant company to prevent competition, dictate prices and shift profits to low tax jurisdictions (concept paper section 7)

triples.name: biased information
triples.description: incomplete or one sided information used as the basis for political and social decisions (concept paper section 4)

triples.name: artificial intelligence
triples.description: Artificial intelligence is the capability of computational systems to perform tasks typically associated with human intelligence, such as learning, reasoning and decision-making.

triples.name: black-box AI
triples.description: proprietary AI systems without disclosed training data, open source code or accountability chain, which reproduce a text in its intended reading instead of exposing its weaknesses (concept paper section 6)

triples.name: citizen participation
triples.description: the missing overview of the solidarity effects of an initiative, which reduces a multifaceted issue to a binary yes or no decision (concept paper section 10)

triples.name: GDP mismeasurement
triples.description: gross domestic product measures the market production and not the benefit, so free goods count as zero and unrepaired damage does not reduce it (concept paper section 11)

triples.name: proprietary software
triples.description: closed source software in the public sector that causes opacity, missing verifiability, vendor dependency and risks to national security (concept paper section 9)

triples.name: climate gas emissions
triples.description: Greenhouse gas emissions are the release of gases into the atmosphere that trap heat and thereby warm the climate.

triples.name: reduce climate gas emissions
triples.description: a transparent, publicly calculated climate tariff that prices the emissions of imports and exports and thereby stops carbon leakage (concept paper section 3)

triples.name: wrong decisions
triples.description: decisions that do not reach the intended goal, e.g. because the knowledge was incomplete

triples.name: avoid wrong decisions
triples.description: decisions based on precise and neutral knowledge instead of the emotional impulse of the group (concept paper section 4)

triples.name: platform regulation
triples.description: democratically legitimised, transparent and justiciable rules against disinformation on internet platforms (concept paper section 2)

triples.name: Delphi method
triples.description: structured, iterative and anonymised consultation of experts, in a real time variant used to let transparent consensus building set the direction instead of the emotional impulse (concept paper section 4)

triples.name: basic income
triples.description: a proto unconditional basic income implemented as a negative income tax, started so low that almost nobody feels an effect and raised as long as the net effect stays positive (concept paper section 5)

triples.name: public AI
triples.description: AI systems with societal decision relevance organised as a public good with disclosed training data, open source availability and clear liability rules (concept paper section 6)

triples.name: market share
triples.description: Market share is the percentage of the total revenue or sales in a market that a company captures.

triples.name: market share tax
triples.description: supplementary taxation of corporate profits linked to the market share in the smallest relevant market segment and levied where the economic use occurs (concept paper section 7)

triples.name: free software
triples.description: free, secure and transparent software in the public sector following the principle public money, public code (concept paper section 9)

triples.name: fluid democracy
triples.description: a structured, argument based and iterative process in which every citizen can propose, debate and decide binding rules (concept paper section 10)

triples.name: domestic usage
triples.description: the actual usage within one country, the base of the gross domestic usage

triples.name: gross domestic usage
triples.description: a measure of the actual usage instead of the market turnover, so that free goods and avoided damage are part of the result (concept paper section 11)

triples.description: the share of the potential loss of a problem that a solution can avoid

triples.description: the work needed to implement a solution the first time, without the recurring operation

triples.name: reward ratio
triples.description: the avoided potential loss per unit of initial effort, used to sort the solutions by efficiency instead of by problem size

triples.name: person year
triples.description: the work of one person during one year, the unit of the initial effort

values.description: about 5 percent of the world GDP: lost labour input and avoidable treatment cost, scaled from the production function effect of Bloom, Canning & Sevilla (2004); health is the factor named most often for happiness (own estimate; the previous value of this file was 13.6, derived from the htp share and not an independent estimate)

the measured -1.04 percent GDP per year over 15 years compounds to about -14 percent in level; applied to the roughly one quarter of the world GDP governed by populist leaders (own estimate; the previous value of this file was 23.8, derived from the htp share and not an independent estimate)

about 2 percent of the world GDP as current annual damage; the long run figure is far higher, this is the loss already realised per year (own estimate; the previous value of this file was 31.5, derived from the htp share and not an independent estimate)

roughly 700 million people below the 2.15 USD line; the gap to a level at which basic needs are met, about 8 USD per person and day (own estimate; the previous value of this file was 20.4, derived from the htp share and not an independent estimate)

about 1.5 percent of the world GDP as deadweight loss from markups, the middle of the range in the markup literature (own estimate; the previous value of this file was 7.3, derived from the htp share and not an independent estimate)

capital misallocation and lost demand; no accepted measurement exists, so this is an order of magnitude only (own estimate; the previous value of this file was 11.2, derived from the htp share and not an independent estimate)

the World Bank present value of the lifetime earnings lost by the current learning poor cohort, annualised over a working life of about 40 years (own estimate; the previous value of this file was 9.4, derived from the htp share and not an independent estimate)

the assumed 30 percent of decisions taken on incomplete information, applied to the part of the public budget where a wrong decision destroys value (own estimate; the previous value of this file was 6.5, derived from the htp share and not an independent estimate)

the assumed 20 percent of the public discourse, valued through its effect on the quality of political decisions (own estimate; the previous value of this file was 8, derived from the htp share and not an independent estimate)

the measured understatement of 0.05 to 0.11 percentage points of growth per year; the loss is the steering error it causes, not the unmeasured value itself (own estimate; the previous value of this file was 2.5, derived from the htp share and not an independent estimate)

wrong decisions taken on unverifiable AI output; the concept paper documents the mechanism but no frequency, so the level is an order of magnitude only (own estimate; the previous value of this file was 4.5, derived from the htp share and not an independent estimate)

the welfare lost because a referendum reduces a multifaceted issue to two positions instead of the assumed twenty (own estimate; the previous value of this file was 3.2, derived from the htp share and not an independent estimate)

the assumed 10 billion EUR of annual public licence spending, extended to the lock-in cost of the wider public and private sector (own estimate; the previous value of this file was 1.8, derived from the htp share and not an independent estimate)

# Global problems ranked by potential loss
 
Companion overview to `solution_prio.json`. Global scope, annual values.
Every figure is given as centre (low - high). The bounds are the 80 percent
probability range and are stored as separate values tagged `low` and `high`;
a value without a range word is the centre.
 
## Ranking
 
| rank | problem | potential loss (trillion EUR / year) | solution | loss reduction | initial effort (person year) | reward ratio |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | health | 5.5 (2.2 – 14) | taxes | 10% (4% – 25%) | 6.0 (2.4 – 15) | 0.09 (0.006 – 1.4) |
| 2 | populism | 4.0 (2.0 – 8.0) | avoid wrong decisions | 100% (40% – 100%) | 8.0 (3.2 – 20) | 0.5 (0.04 – 2.5) |

| 5 | market power | 1.6 (0.64 – 4.0) | market share tax | 30% (12% – 75%) | 2.0 (0.8 – 5.0) | 0.24 (0.02 – 3.8) |
| 6 | wealth concentration | 1.4 (0.47 – 4.2) | basic income | 30% (12% – 75%) | 5.0 (2.0 – 12) | 0.08 (0.004 – 1.6) |
| 7 | education | 0.55 (0.22 – 1.4) | spending | 5% (2% – 12.5%) | 6.0 (2.4 – 15) | 0.005 (0.0003 – 0.07) |
| 8 | biased information | 0.45 (0.15 – 1.4) | Delphi method | 15% (6% – 37.5%) | 4.0 (1.6 – 10) | 0.02 (0.0009 – 0.32) |
| 9 | disinformation | 0.35 (0.12 – 1.1) | platform regulation | 10% (4% – 25%) | 12 (4.8 – 30) | 0.003 (0.0002 – 0.05) |
| 10 | GDP mismeasurement | 0.25 (0.1 – 0.62) | gross domestic usage | 100% (40% – 100%) | 4.0 (1.6 – 10) | 0.06 (0.004 – 0.39) |
| 11 | black-box AI | 0.22 (0.07 – 0.66) | public AI | 50% (20% – 100%) | 20 (8.0 – 50) | 0.005 (0.0003 – 0.08) |
| 12 | citizen participation | 0.18 (0.06 – 0.54) | fluid democracy | 50% (20% – 100%) | 6.0 (2.4 – 15) | 0.01 (0.0008 – 0.23) |
| 13 | proprietary software | 0.1 (0.04 – 0.25) | free software | 50% (20% – 100%) | 1.0 (0.4 – 2.5) | 0.05 (0.003 – 0.62) |
 
## Probability range
 
The range is not a measured dispersion. It is derived from the confidence of the
value by a multiplicative factor around the centre, `[x / f, x * f]`:
 
| kind of value | factor |
| --- | ---: |
| taken from a source, not assumed | 1.2 |
| assumed, confidence at least 0.25 | 2.0 |
| assumed, confidence 0.15 to 0.25 | 2.5 |
| assumed, confidence below 0.15 | 3.0 |
| definitional or structural | 1.5 |
 
Shares are clamped at 1, which is why the loss reduction of populism and of GDP
mismeasurement has an upper bound equal to its centre. Confidence values carry no
range of their own. The factor table is itself an assumption: it makes the ranges
comparable across the file, but it does not make any single range empirical, and
two values with the same factor are not equally well known.
 
## Reward ratio
 
`reward ratio = potential loss * loss reduction / initial effort`
 
The range of the ratio combines the worst corner (low loss, low reduction, high
effort) with the best corner (high loss, high reduction, low effort). This is a
corner combination and not a convolution, so the interval is far wider than 80
percent: it assumes the three errors move together, which is the pessimistic
reading. The ranges of all thirteen problems overlap, so the ranking by reward
ratio is not resolved by this data. Only the distance between populism at the top
and poverty at the bottom survives the overlap.
 
The initial effort remains the weakest column: no source contains it, every
figure is an own order of magnitude estimate with a uniform confidence of 0.2.
The two loss reduction figures at the share limit are the weakest rows: populism
assumes that the solution fully offsets the measured GDP decline, which is what
the value in `problem_populism.json` implies but is a very strong claim for a
knowledge infrastructure.
 
Two errors of the earlier data should be corrected independently of this table:
health and poverty are swapped both in the potential loss and in the potential
gain. The htp shares give -0.24 for health and -0.16 for poverty, which yield
20.4 and 13.6, while the file carried 13.6 for health and 20.4 for poverty.
